name: Wedding
subtitle: Guest, bride & reception
dressing: Go rich: silk, brocade, velvet and full-length silhouettes. Day weddings suit lighter silks and pastels; evening weddings can take jewel tones and heavier embroidery.
whatToWear: Banarasi or Kanjeevaram sarees, lehengas, floor-length anarkalis, saree gowns for the reception.
avoid: Bridal red if you are a guest, all-white or all-black at many Hindu weddings (check with the hosts), and short hemlines.
colours: Emerald, wine, royal blue, rani pink, gold.

name: Sangeet
subtitle: Music & dance night
dressing: You will dance, so pick something light that moves and catches the light. Shimmer and sequins are welcome.
whatToWear: Pre-draped or ruffle sarees, sharara sets, light lehengas, dhoti-pant sets, cape sets.
avoid: Heavy trailing dupattas, stiff silk that restricts movement and very high heels.

name: Mehendi
subtitle: Henna day
dressing: Comfort first: you will sit for a while with henna drying on your hands and feet.
whatToWear: Mirror-work lehengas, sharara or gharara sets, short kurtas with palazzos.
avoid: Long or tight sleeves (they smudge henna) and fabrics that show stains.

name: Haldi
subtitle: Turmeric ceremony
dressing: Expect to get turmeric on you. Wear washable cotton or georgette you do not mind staining.
whatToWear: Yellow kurta sets with gota work, simple cotton lehengas, floral jewellery.
avoid: Expensive silk, white and anything dry-clean only.
colours: Turmeric yellow, marigold, mustard, white with yellow.

name: Festivals
subtitle: Diwali, Eid, Navratri, Onam, Puja
dressing: Traditional with a sense of celebration. Navratri means twirl-ready chaniya cholis, Onam means ivory and gold kasavu, Durga Puja means red and white.
whatToWear: Silk sarees, anarkalis, sharara sets, chaniya cholis, kurta sets.
avoid: Synthetic fabrics near diyas and candles, and dark dull colours.

name: Pooja & Temple
subtitle: Prayers & ceremonies
dressing: Modest and traditional. Shoulders and knees covered, breathable fabric for sitting on the floor.
whatToWear: Cotton or silk sarees, chikankari kurta sets, half sarees, mekhela chador.
avoid: Leather belts and bags at many temples, sleeveless tops, short dresses.
colours: Ivory, saffron, red, yellow, temple green.

name: Office
subtitle: Everyday work
dressing: Polished, comfortable and repeatable. Neat fits and solid colours with one print at most.
whatToWear: Cotton kurta sets, handloom sarees, pantsuits, pencil skirts, shirt dresses, wrap dresses.
avoid: Heavy embroidery, sheer fabric, sequins and very loud prints.
colours: Navy, ivory, camel, grey, muted pastels.

name: Interview
subtitle: First impressions
dressing: Look capable and calm. Structured pieces, neutral colours and minimal jewellery.
whatToWear: Power pantsuit, pencil skirt with a silk blouse, a crisp kurta with straight pants.
avoid: Bright prints, strong perfume and new shoes you have not broken in.

name: Date Night
subtitle: Dinner for two
dressing: Something you feel good in that is easy to sit and walk in. One standout detail is enough.
whatToWear: Slip dress, wrap dress, jumpsuit, off-shoulder top with flares, the little black dress.
avoid: Outfits you need to keep adjusting and shoes you cannot walk in.

name: Brunch & Day Out
subtitle: Daytime casual
dressing: Fresh, relaxed and photo-friendly. Prints and light fabrics shine in daylight.
whatToWear: Sundresses, co-ord sets, kurta with jeans, kaftans, pleated skirts.

name: Party & Night Out
subtitle: Clubs & celebrations
dressing: Go bold. Shine, cut-outs and strong colour all work after dark.
whatToWear: Sequin minis, bodycon dresses, jumpsuits, party sarees, dhoti-pant sets.
avoid: Daywear cottons that wrinkle and flat, dull colours.
colours: Hot pink, cobalt, silver, black, gold.

name: Cocktail & Reception
subtitle: Dressy evenings
dressing: Between formal and party: elegant with some sparkle. Indo-western fusion is perfect here.
whatToWear: Saree gowns, cape sets, satin slip dresses, sequin sarees, evening gowns.
avoid: Very casual denim and overly bridal pieces.

name: Formal & Gala
subtitle: Black-tie events
dressing: Floor-length and refined. Fit matters more than embellishment.
whatToWear: Evening gowns, mermaid gowns, Kanjeevaram sarees, saree gowns.
avoid: Short hemlines, casual fabrics and chunky everyday sneakers.

name: Travel
subtitle: Airports & sightseeing
dressing: Layers, pockets and fabrics that do not crease. Comfortable shoes are not optional.
whatToWear: Co-ords, kurta with jeans, trench coat over jeans, athleisure, maxi dresses.
avoid: Delicate fabrics, lots of jewellery and stiff new shoes.
colours: Neutrals, denim, olive, one bright accent.

name: College & Everyday
subtitle: Classes & hangouts
dressing: Easy, expressive and budget-friendly. Mix basics so a few pieces make many outfits.
whatToWear: Jeans with tees, kurta with jeans, block-print kurta sets, athleisure, pleated skirts.
avoid: Anything precious you cannot sit on the grass in.
colours: Anything you love: denim, white, bright accents.

name: Beach & Vacation
subtitle: Sun, sand & resorts
dressing: Breathable, flowy and quick-drying. Prints and bright colour look great against water and sand.
whatToWear: Kaftans, boho maxi dresses, sundresses, linen co-ords.
avoid: Heavy fabrics, dark colours that absorb heat and heels in sand.
